config.title: Build refresh token rotation flow

intro.title: Build refresh token rotation flow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure refresh token rotation flow for a Node.js application. You will learn how to automatically issue new access tokens using a refresh token when the old one expires, enhancing security by reducing token reuse. The core programming concepts involve managing JWT (JSON Web Token) validation, state handling for tokens, and implementing conditional logic for token refresh. You will work with JavaScript, the jsonwebtoken library, and HTTP headers to handle authentication tokens. By the end, you'll have a functional flow that rotates tokens to keep user sessions secure without requiring frequent logins.
intro.usecase: Refresh token rotation is a critical security pattern used in virtually every modern web application that maintains user sessions. When you stay logged into platforms like Gmail, Netflix, or banking dashboards for extended periods, your access tokens expire periodically, but the app seamlessly refreshes them in the background without requiring you to re-enter credentials. This flow ensures continuous, secure access in admin panels, e-commerce platforms, and collaborative tools where users interact with data-rich interfaces for hours. As a Node.js developer, implementing this properly prevents session hijacking while delivering the smooth, uninterrupted experience users expect from professional applications.

objectives: Implement a refresh token endpoint in a Node.js server
Configure token validation middleware to check refresh token expiration
Initialize a new access token when a valid refresh token is presented
Manipulate token payloads to include user identification data
Integrate refresh token rotation into an existing authentication flow
Apply secure storage practices for refresh tokens in a database
Control token refresh frequency to prevent abuse

steps.title: Create login simulation function
steps.instruction: Create a function named loginUser that takes a username parameter and returns an object containing both an access token and a refresh token for that user.
steps.hint: Inside the function, call your existing generateAccessToken function to create the access token, then generate a refresh token similarly. Store the refresh token in the refreshTokens object with the username as the key, then return both tokens.
steps.expectedOutcome: A loginUser function that generates tokens and stores the refresh token, returning both in an object.
successCriteria: The loginUser function exists, takes a username parameter, generates both tokens, stores the refresh token in refreshTokens[username], and returns an object with accessToken and refreshToken properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function generates both tokens, stores the refresh token in the refreshTokens object, and returns them in an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loginUser function is missing or doesn't meet the requirements. It should take a username, generate both tokens, store the refresh token, and return an object with both tokens.

steps.title: Create access token validation function
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateAccessToken that takes an access token string as a parameter and returns true if the token is valid (not expired) and false otherwise. For now, implement a simple expiration check by verifying the token exists in your storage and hasn't expired (use a hardcoded expiration time of 1 hour from token creation).
steps.hint: You can check if a token exists by looking it up in your token storage object. For expiration, you can store a timestamp when the token was created and compare it with the current time.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateAccessToken function that checks token existence and expiration, returning a boolean.
successCriteria: The validateAccessToken function exists, accepts a token parameter, checks if the token exists in refreshTokens, verifies it hasn't expired (within 1 hour), and returns true/false accordingly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly checks both token existence and expiration. Remember to compare the token's creation time with the current time.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation function doesn't seem to be working correctly. Check that you're looking up the token in your refreshTokens object and comparing timestamps properly.

steps.title: Create refresh token validation function
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateRefreshToken that takes a refreshToken string as a parameter and returns true if the token exists in the refreshTokens object, otherwise returns false.
steps.hint: Check if the provided refreshToken exists as a key in the refreshTokens object you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateRefreshToken function that checks token existence in the refreshTokens object.
successCriteria: The validateRefreshToken function exists, takes a refreshToken parameter, and returns a boolean based on whether the token exists in refreshTokens.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function takes a refreshToken parameter and returns true/false based on whether it exists in refreshTokens.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validateRefreshToken function should check if the provided token exists in the refreshTokens object and return a boolean.

steps.title: Create token rotation handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named rotateRefreshToken that takes a refreshToken parameter, validates it, and returns a new access/refresh token pair.
steps.hint: Inside the function, first check if the refreshToken exists in your refreshTokens object. If valid, generate new tokens and update the storage.
steps.expectedOutcome: A rotateRefreshToken function that implements the core refresh token rotation logic.
successCriteria: The rotateRefreshToken function exists, validates the refreshToken parameter, generates new tokens, updates the refreshTokens object, and returns the new token pair.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the rotateRefreshToken function, but make sure it validates the token, generates new tokens, updates storage, and returns the new pair.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rotateRefreshToken function is missing or incomplete. Review the token rotation logic.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Update token storage to use file persistence
steps.instruction: Modify the refreshTokens object initialization to load existing tokens from the tokens.json file if it exists, using a try-catch block.
steps.hint: Use fs.readFileSync inside a try block to read the file, parse it as JSON, and assign it to refreshTokens. In the catch block, initialize refreshTokens as an empty object if the file doesn't exist.
steps.expectedOutcome: The refreshTokens variable will be initialized with data from tokens.json if the file exists, otherwise it will be an empty object.
successCriteria: refreshTokens is declared with let, initialized inside a try-catch block that attempts to read and parse tokens.json, and falls back to an empty object on error.
